rules.name: scale
rules.rule: the Mexican-hat (Ricker) scale a, in seconds; CWT normalised by 1/a (the paper uses 1/sqrt(a)), wavelet truncated to +/- 5a (Du, Kibbe & Lin 2006)

rules.name: best_scale_s
rules.rule: the scale at which the ridge's coefficient is largest, refined by a parabola in log-scale through the top three ridge points

rules.name: duration_s
rules.rule: FWHM of a Gaussian bump whose Ricker response peaks at best_scale_s: duration_s = 2*sqrt(ln 2) * best_scale_s = 1.665 * best_scale_s

rules.name: cwt_duration_s
rules.rule: the same as duration_s, under a name Event shape does not overwrite (its own duration_s is onset to recovery)

rules.name: span
rules.rule: peak_idx +/- duration_s (twice the FWHM), clipped to the span

rules.name: snr
rules.rule: detectability at the event's own scale: the largest coefficient on the ridge (within the event's scale band) / noise, where noise = 1.96 x 1.4826 x MAD of the coefficients at the event's best scale in a window of max(noise_window_s, +/- 30 scales) around the peak less +/- 4 scales around it, floored at the span's smallest-scale noise scaled to that scale as white noise (x sqrt(a_min / a))

rules.name: noise_min_scale
rules.rule: diagnostic only (the paper's noise): the 95th percentile of |coefficients| at the smallest scale in a noise_window_s window around the peak; not used to accept events

rules.name: coefficient baseline
rules.rule: each scale's coefficients minus their running median over +/- 10 scales, so a curved drift (which the hat does not cancel) goes and an event stays

rules.name: peak_idx
rules.rule: the ridge's position at the smallest scale of the event's band whose coefficient is still >= half the event's peak (span-relative)

rules.name: ridge_scales
rules.rule: number of scales the ridge has a maximum on (gaps excluded)

rules.name: polarity
rules.rule: +1 spike (a maximum of the coefficients), -1 drop (a maximum of the negated coefficients) — Event shape's encoding; ridge_polarity says it in words and survives Event shape, which re-measures `polarity`

rules.name: edge_flag
rules.rule: the wavelet's support at best_scale_s (+/- 5a) crosses a span edge, where the trace was extended by odd reflection

rules.name: side lobe
rules.rule: a candidate is dropped when, at its own best scale, the opposite polarity reaches >= 1/0.6 times its coefficient within 2.5 scales of it (the hat's negative lobes are 0.45 of its peak)

rules.name: nested
rules.rule: every maximum of a ridge's coefficient profile over scale that passes min_snr and stands >= 1 x the local noise above its saddle is its own event (a fast event on a slow one)

rules.name: step_pair
rules.rule: at the event's best scale, an opposite-polarity coefficient within 2.5 scales is between 0.6 and 1/0.6 of its own: it may be one corner of an abrupt edge (a sharkfin's fall), not an event of its own

rules.name: duplicate
rules.rule: of two same-polarity events closer than half a scale with best scales within 1.5x, the stronger is kept
